Notebook introduction

This document provides a comprehensive technical breakdown of the **Transform, Anchor, and Pivot Subsystem** in the Retiam WebGPU Engine. It details the mathematical foundations, continuous local anchoring vs. absolute world pivoting, type definitions ([`Constants.ts`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/_core/Constants.ts)), low-level matrix transformations ([`Transform.ts`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/_core/Transform.ts)), entity declarative layout ([`Entity.ts`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/_core/Entity.ts)), and state synchronization during animation ([`Animator.ts`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/animation/Animator.ts), [`GroupAnimator.ts`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/animation/GroupAnimator.ts), [`AnimationFunctions.ts`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/animation/AnimationFunctions.ts)).

blocks.text: 2. Resolving the Ambiguity: Anchor vs. Pivot
A core design challenge in 2D/3D scene graphs is distinguishing between:

items: **Local Bounding-Box Anchor (`anchor`)**: Coordinates expressed relative to the entity's own bounding box dimensions. Here, `[0, 0, 0]` represents the geometric center of the entity's AABB.
**Absolute World Pivot (`pivot`)**: Coordinates expressed in world space. Here, `[0, 0, 0]` represents the scene's global center.

blocks.text: Previously, using `ORIGIN` (`[0, 0, 0]`) created ambiguity: users inspecting `ORIGIN` saw `[0, 0, 0]` and could confuse the entity's local center with the world origin.

4. Mathematical Foundations
A. Continuous Anchor to Local Point Mapping
An anchor $a = (a_x, a_y, a_z) \in [-1, 1]^3$ maps linearly across the entity's local bounding box $[x_{min}, x_{max}] \times [y_{min}, y_{max}] \times [z_{min}, z_{max}]$:

Because $a$ is continuous, users are not restricted to predefined constants (`UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `UL`, `UR`, `DL`, `DR`). Any intermediate value (e.g. `[0, 0.25, 0]`) computes the exact fractional boundary point.

7. Animation System Integration ([Animator.ts](../src/engine/animation/Animator.ts) & [GroupAnimator.ts](../src/engine/animation/GroupAnimator.ts))

During animations, the transform state operates on two endpoints: `start` and `target`. When an animation specifies an anchor or pivot, the system evaluates the anchor in the target state and keeps start/target pivot offsets synchronized:
Multi-Entity Group Pivoting ([GroupAnimator.ts](../src/engine/animation/GroupAnimator.ts))

For groups (`VGroup` / [`GroupAnimator`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/animation/GroupAnimator.ts)), local anchors are evaluated against the **combined collective bounding box** of all child entities:
All children in the group are then transformed in unison around this shared centroid or edge anchor.
